subject.title: fix(baseten): reject malformed model metadata numbers

question: Should Baseten string metadata deliberately reject exponent-form and whitespace-padded numeric strings, using bundled catalog values instead, or should the accepted string grammar preserve any provider-supported numeric representations?
rationale: The implementation is mechanically sound for its stated policy, but accepting or rejecting valid provider string representations is a compatibility contract choice rather than a purely local parsing decision.

options.title: Confirm strict canonical strings
options.body: Merge after confirming that decimal-only, unpadded strings are the intended Baseten string-metadata contract and refresh the branch against current `main`.

options.title: Broaden the accepted grammar
options.body: Revise the parser and tests to accept any documented Baseten numeric-string representation while still rejecting JavaScript-only coercion forms such as hexadecimal.

recommendation.title: Confirm strict canonical strings
recommendation.body: Merge after confirming that decimal-only, unpadded strings are the intended Baseten string-metadata contract and refresh the branch against current `main`.
